items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: George Boyd played with us a while. ... Jack Carey, myself, George Foster, Little Chinese, George Boyd.

ctx.x: And who did he have in his band?

Well they had, I don't know what this tipping guy name on trombone, there's a tip when he wore, a dark fella. And Dave on drum and me on trumpet, well he was different clarinet players. You never had the same clarinet players, you know. George Boyd played with us a while. What's the name, Little Pill? Cripple Pill. Yeah. Let's see, did they have a guitar at the band?
A banjo? Yeah, a banjo. You know the banjo play out there, I forget.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: such as George Boyd, Walter Preston, Joe Gable, and Aidy Morris. And we got a little band together there

ctx.x: Very good idea. So, my first man I worked with here was a fellow named Jack Kerri. We supposed to invent a tagger rag. And we did very nice around New Orleans, so some of the boys in the band decided me to get my own band, such as George Boyd, Walter Preston, Joe Gable, and Aidy Morris. And we got a little band together there, and we really did fine, fine, until the same thing like now, come up Lent, and we all got a job. I didn't have any when I called them to play. They couldn't go. So, I just thought I'd move…
Now tell us, how did you get your name Punch? How did you get that nickname?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: I said like uh, George Boyd and Zeb, what's his name, Zeb?

ctx.x: I said like uh, George Boyd and Zeb, what's his name, Zeb?
